```{r}
#| include: false

source("R/efile_helpers.R")

rel     <- efile_release("pf_v3_1")
rel_990 <- efile_current("990")
cc      <- efile_concordance()
counts  <- efile_nonempty(efile_counts(rel))
meta    <- efile_table_meta(counts$table, cc, rel$form)
cov     <- efile_coverage(efile_counts(rel_990), efile_counts(rel))
fil     <- efile_filings(counts)
yrs     <- range(counts$year)
```

The NCCS 990-PF Efile database turns the Form 990-PF returns that private foundations file electronically with the IRS into `r length(unique(counts$table))` relational tables, one or more for each Part of the form and its attached statements. Every table is published for each tax year in two formats, **CSV** and **Parquet**.

| | |
|:--|:--|
| **Release** | `r efile_label(rel)` (published `r rel$published`) |
| **Returns** | Form 990-PF (private foundations and section 4947(a)(1) charitable trusts) |
| **Tax years** | `r yrs[1]`&ndash;`r yrs[2]` (`r yrs[2]` is a partial year) |
| **Tables** | `r length(unique(counts$table))` tables, `r fmt_n(nrow(counts))` table-year files |
| **Filings** | `r fmt_n(sum(fil$rows_tot))` returns |
| **Labels** | concordance990 `r cc$version` |
| **Public charities** | Form 990 and 990-EZ returns are a separate database: [`r efile_label(rel_990)` catalog](`r rel_990$page`) |

## About this release {#about}

### Data sources and processing

The Taxpayer First Act of 2019 made electronic filing mandatory for Form 990-PF for tax years beginning after July 1, 2019, so recent waves cover nearly every private foundation; earlier years include only foundations that chose to e-file. NCCS builds the database from the XML files indexed by the [Giving Tuesday 990 Data Commons](https://www.givingtuesday.org/data-commons/990-data-infrastructure/), supplemented with returns the IRS e-file index lists but the Data Commons index never picked up (see the release notes below).

Each XML element (xpath) is assigned to a research variable and a table by the **Master Concordance** ([concordance990](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/concordance990/)), and the tables are built with the [ef2](https://nonprofit-open-data-collective.github.io/ef2/) package. A table holds one Part of the form: either one row per filing (**1:1**), or several rows per filing for repeating groups such as officers, grants paid, or capital gains (**1:M**). Tables in Part 99 hold the statements foundations attach to the return (accounting fees, depreciation, other investments, and so on).

The database also carries the two tables shared by every e-filed return: the filing header (`F9-P00-T00-HEADER`) and the signature block (`F9-P02-T00-SIGNATURE`). Here they hold 990-PF filings only. `F9_00_ORG_EXEMPT_TYPE` in the header is empty for 990-PF returns.

Efile data are organized by **tax year**, the year in which the foundation's fiscal year begins (`TAX_PERIOD_BEGIN_DATE`). The IRS releases returns in monthly batches, so the most recent tax year is always incomplete. Form 990-PF was renumbered in 2023 (Part VI became Part V, and so on); the tables follow the pre-2023 numbering, and the part titles below give both.

Every table carries the keys needed to join tables to each other and to the BMF: `OBJECTID` (`OID-` followed by 18 digits, one per filing), `EIN2`, and `TAX_YEAR`. One-to-many tables add `TABLE_ID` (`TID-NNN-NNN-NNN`, one per row). Every row also carries `URL`, a link to the source XML return.

## Table and file names {#file-names}

Table names follow the pattern **FF-PPP-TTT-NAME**, and each file appends the tax year: `PF-P15-T01-SUPPLEMENTARY-INFO-GRANT-PAID-2023.parquet`.

- **FF** is the form: `PF` = Form 990-PF; `F9` marks the two shared header tables.
- **PPP** is the part: `P01` = Part I, `P02` = Part II, and so on. `P00` is the heading and `P99` holds attached statements.
- **TTT** is the table: `T00` holds the one-to-one fields of the part, and `T01`, `T02`, ... are its one-to-many tables.

Each table-year is published as **CSV** (readable anywhere) and **Parquet** (smaller and much faster in R with `arrow` or `duckdb`; panel990 reads Parquet by default). Both files hold the same rows and columns. Table-years with no filings are omitted from the listings below.
